_comment: background-clip crossed with border-radius — the second consumer of the css-backgrounds-3 §5.3 corner-reduction rule (the inner curve radius is the outer radius minus the border width, then minus the padding for the content box, floored at 0 at each step), applied here to the background PAINTING AREA rather than to a clip. Neither `background-clip` nor `background-origin` appears in fixtures/visual-test.json, and the existing fixtures/properties/background/background-clip.json uses no border-radius at all, so the reduction is unexercised. Construction note that matters: the border is `solid transparent`, not dashed. A dashed border is the usual way to reveal what is painted underneath, but dash phase and corner joins are themselves a divergence source and would confound the measurement; a transparent border reveals the same thing with nothing to disagree about. Boxes are content 160x60 with padding 10px and a 12px border, so the border box is 204x104, the padding box 180x80 at (12,12), the content box 160x60 at (22,22). Coordinates below are component-local (the web canvas adds (16,16)); the harness block-font label occupies y in [6,13) from x=8, so all sample points are taken at y=52. MUST DIFFER, pairwise, all four of BorderBox / PaddingBox / ContentBox / PaddingBox_NoRadius. BCR_BorderBox_OpaqueBorder is a geometry control, not a variant: if a platform drops zero-alpha borders from layout, the first five rows shrink to 180x80 while it stays 204x104, which localises the fault to layout rather than to background-clip.

BCR_BorderBox._note: background-clip: border-box (the initial value). §5.2 factor is 1 (adjacent radius sums 60 <= 204 and 60 <= 104). EXPECTED: blue fills the whole 204x104 border box with 30px corners, right out to the outer edge, because the border is transparent. Samples: (102,52) blue · (2,52) blue (mid-height falls on the straight part of the left edge, between the two 30px arcs) · (2,2) canvas #1A1A2E.

BCR_PaddingBox._note: Only background-clip changes. Padding box is 180x80 at (12,12); §5.3 gives it radius 30 - 12 = 18. EXPECTED: blue 180x80 with 18px corners inside a 12px transparent band. Samples: (6,52) canvas #1A1A2E (inside the border band) · (102,52) blue. DISCRIMINATOR against BCR_BorderBox: the 12px band must go dark.

BCR_ContentBox._note: Content box is 160x60 at (22,22); §5.3 reduces again by the padding: 18 - 10 = 8. EXPECTED: blue 160x60 with 8px corners inside a 22px dark band. Samples: (16,52) canvas #1A1A2E · (102,52) blue. A platform that reduces once but not twice paints these corners at 18px.

BCR_PaddingBox_NoRadius._note: Same clip box as BCR_PaddingBox with border-radius: 0. EXPECTED: a SHARP blue 180x80 at (12,12). It must differ from BCR_PaddingBox by 4 * (18^2 - pi*18^2/4) = 4 * 69.53 = 278 px. If the two render identically, that platform ignores border-radius when clipping the background — a silent drop no cross-platform comparison would see if all three did it.

BCR_PaddingBox_ZeroFloor._note: The floor case: border 40px, outer radius 20px, padding 0, so the padding-box radius is max(0, 20 - 40) = 0. Border box 180x120, padding box 100x40 at (40,40). EXPECTED: a SHARP blue 100x40 rectangle. DISCRIMINATOR: any rounded blue corner means the floor is missing (|20-40| and clamp-to-20 both round it). The label sits at (8,6), outside the blue rect, over canvas colour.

BCR_BorderBox_OpaqueBorder._note: GEOMETRY CONTROL, not a variant of the property. Same box as BCR_BorderBox with an opaque yellow border. EXPECTED: 204x104 overall; a 12px #f1c40f ring with a 30px outer curve; blue inside it with an 18px inner curve. With an opaque border, border-box and padding-box clipping are indistinguishable by construction — that is the point: this row pins the border-box SIZE independently of the property under test.
